//: A proposal. The project owner copies this text to the file that dispatch.json names under buildersProfiles and edits it by hand; no agent creates or changes it. A key that starts with // is a note and is not read.
//how: dispatch.ps1 -Profile <name> passes the profile's allow rules with --allowedTools and its deny rules with --disallowedTools, on top of the builders' settings file. A profile only adds: the shared deny list is always passed and a deny always wins, so no profile removes a shared deny. Scope a write with Edit(path), never Write(path): a Write(path) rule matches nothing.
//baseSettings: Optional, per profile. A settings file, from the main checkout, passed on --settings in place of the shared builders' file. Use one when a profile must allow less than the shared file: the shared file allows bare Edit and Write, and a profile's rules only add. The script refuses a base file that is missing or lacks any shared deny rule. Start it from templates/research.settings.example.json.

profiles.//research: A standing profile for findings-only tickets: web search, any web page, read-only repo tools, issue comments. No probe script, no push, no gh pr, and writes only under builder-state/ (its base file has no bare Edit or Write).
profiles.//probe: A standing profile with exactly one probe rule: the fixed path builder-state/probe.py, no argument, no wildcard, never builder-state/*.py. The builder writes that script, and it enforces its own ALLOWED_HOSTS on every request and every redirect hop. The brief names the hosts; the manager reads the script against them at closeout. A script that changes data is not a probe. This rule never goes in the shared builders' file or in the research profile.
